name: Project overview
description:
1. Explored codx-junior's existing documentation machinery (`WikiManager`, `WikiDomains`, `WikiIndex`, `DependencyGraph`, `background.process_project_wiki`).
2. Found gaps: no README generation, no agent resources (`AGENTS.md`, `llms.txt`, `CONTEXT.md`), no orchestrator or manifest, plus dead stub code (`KnowledgeWiki`, `WikiEngine.process_wiki_changes`).
3. Wrote a spec at `codx/junior/wiki/DOCUMENTATION_ENGINE.md` defining a unified Documentation Engine for humans **and** agents.
4. Spec covers a `DocumentationResource` contract, resource catalog, `plan/build/refresh` pipeline, API surface, config flags, and implementation plan.
5. Open questions: preferred naming/location for the engine, and confirming the `docs_auto_rebuild` budget guard before implementing step 1.

Wiki, readme and other resources engine to generate project's documentation for humans and agents

Codx-junior must be able to keep any project documented for humans and agents llms.

I'll explore the project structure to understand the codebase and how documentation generation is (or should be) implemented. ``` Search completed: 5 queries executed, 50 documents found ``` Let me read the key wiki-related files to understand the current implementation. ``` Read 7 file(s) | Successfully read: codx/junior/wiki/wiki_manager.py, codx/junior/wiki/wiki_domains.py, codx/junior/wiki/wiki_index.py, codx/junior/wiki/README.md, codx/junior/engine/wiki_engine.py, codx/junior/knowledge/knowledge_wiki.py, codx/junior/background.py ``` Let me examine the settings, API layer, change manager, and the wiki model to understand the full picture. ``` Read 3 file(s) | Successfully read: codx/junior/wiki/model.py, codx/junior/changes/change_manager.py, codx/junior/engine/session.py ``` ``` Search completed: 6 queries executed, 60 documents found ``` Let me look at the wiki template, settings model fields, dependency graph, and any existing agent-oriented resources. ``` Read 5 file(s) | Successfully read: codx/junior/wiki/wiki_template/index.md, codx/junior/wiki/wiki_template/.vitepress/config.mts, codx/junior/wiki/wiki_template/wiki-manager.sh, codx/junior/wiki/wiki_template/package.json, codx/junior/knowledge/knowledge_graph.py ``` ``` Search completed: 8 queries executed, 80 documents found ``` I now have a complete picture of the existing documentation machinery in codx-junior. Let me capture what exists and design the missing "resources engine" as a structured specification document. ``` Read 2 file(s) | Successfully read: codx/junior/profiles/agent-coding-task.md, codx/junior/profiles/wiki.profile ``` I have everything I need. Here is a structured specification document for the engine, which unifies, extends, and closes the gaps I found in the current code. I'll save it into the wiki module folder. ```md codx/junior/wiki/DOCUMENTATION_ENGINE.md # Documentation Engine — Wiki, README & Agent Resources > **Goal:** codx-junior must be able to keep **any** project documented — continuously > and automatically — for **two audiences at once**: > > - 🧑💻 **Humans** — onboarding, architecture, how to run, how to contribute. > - 🤖 **Agents / LLMs** — machine-readable context, boundaries, conventions and entry points. > > This document specifies the *resources* the engine produces, how they are generated, > how they relate to the existing code, and what still needs to be built. --- ## 1. Why a dedicated engine Documentation is currently split across several ad-hoc pieces (see §4). Each piece knows a little about the project but there is no single component that answers: * *What documentation does this project need?* * *Who is it for — a human or an agent?* * *When is it stale, and how do I refresh it?* The **Documentation Engine** is that single orchestrator. It treats every output as a **resource** derived from one shared understanding of the project (files, dependency graph, domains, knowledge base). ### Design principles | # | Principle | Rationale | |---|-----------|-----------| | 1 | **Single source of truth** | All resources derive from the same model: file list + dependency graph + domain map + knowledge DB. | | 2 | **Two audiences, explicit targets** | Each resource declares `audience: human \| agent \| both`. | | 3 | **Incremental first** | A single file change updates only the affected resources. | | 4 | **Idempotent & re-runnable** | `rebuild` always converges to the same result. | | 5 | **Agent-parseable** | Agent resources are short, deterministic, link-rich and section-stable. | | 6 | **Never lock the user in** | Generated files live in the project and are plain Markdown/JSON — editable and diff-able. | --- ## 2. The resources ```mermaid mindmap root((Documentation Engine)) Human Wiki README.md CONTRIBUTING.md Agent AGENTS.md llms.txt CONTEXT.md Shared Domain pages Module pages wiki_index.json dependency_graph.json ``` ### 2.1 Human resources
📚 Wiki — <codx_path>/wiki/** or project_wiki_path A navigable, multi-page site (VitePress/MkDocs) built from three layers: * **Home** (`home.md`) — high-level overview only, no implementation detail. * **Categories** — a 6-branch tree of the project's functional areas (AI-generated, refreshed from the domain map). * **Domain pages** (`domains/.md`) — one page per detected code domain, with `Overview / Files in Domain / Dependencies / Used By / Entry Points`. * **Module pages** (`modules/.md`) — one page per file, with `Overview / Exported Symbols / Dependencies / Usage Examples`. _Already implemented in `WikiManager`, `WikiDomains`, `WikiIndex`._
📄 README.md — project root The front door for humans **and** the first thing an agent crawls. Must contain, in order: 1. What the project is (1 paragraph). 2. Badges (build, license, version). 3. Quick start (install → run in ≤ 5 commands). 4. Feature list. 5. Links to the Wiki, AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md. _Not implemented yet — README is only **read** today (`FileEngine.get_readme`)._
🤝 CONTRIBUTING.md — project root How to set up a dev environment, run tests, lint, and open a PR. Derived from `project_scripts`, detected tooling (package.json, pyproject.toml, Makefile) and the `software_developer` profile. _Not implemented yet._
### 2.2 Agent resources
🤖 AGENTS.md — project root The rules-of-engagement file that modern coding agents read first. Stable sections: ```md # AGENTS.md ## Project map # top-level folders → one line each ## Build & test # exact commands (from project_scripts) ## Conventions # language, formatting, import style, naming ## Where things live # domain → folder → entry point ## Do # safe actions ## Don't # never touch generated/ dirs, secrets, lockfiles ## Definition of done # tests to pass, docs to update ``` This mirrors the existing `agent-coding-task.md` profile and the `search`/`code` tool contract, but as a project-level contract. _Not implemented yet._
🔗 llms.txt — project root (llmstxt.org convention) A compact, link-first plain-text index that any LLM can consume in one fetch: ```txt # codx-junior > AI sidekick that keeps any project documented and tested. ## Docs - [Wiki home](/wiki/home.md): full documentation - [AGENTS.md](/AGENTS.md): agent rules - [Architecture](/wiki/domains/architecture.md): code domains ## Optional - [domain_map.json](/.codx/domain_map.json): machine-readable domains - [wiki_index.json](/wiki/wiki_index.json): machine-readable index ``` _Not implemented yet._
🧠 CONTEXT.md — <codx_path>/CONTEXT.md A dense, always-current "brain dump" for agent prompts: the project profile + the current domain map + recent knowledge highlights. Populated by `Knowledge.get_project_summary()`. _Partially exists (`/api/knowledge/summary`)._
### 2.3 Shared / machine resources | Resource | Path | Purpose | |----------|------|---------| | `dependency_graph.json` | `/` | Files → imports / imported_by / external_deps. ✅ exists | | `domain_map.json` | `/` | Detected domains with files, entry points, keywords. ✅ exists | | `wiki_index.json` | `/` | Files + domains index, also pushed to Milvus. ✅ exists | | `doc_manifest.json` | `/` | **NEW** — registry of every generated resource, audience, hash & timestamp. | --- ## 3. Architecture The engine sits between the **knowledge layer** (inputs) and the **API** (control surface), and reuses the existing `WikiManager` as its wiki backend. ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph Inputs KB[Knowledge DB] DG[DependencyGraph] DM[domain_map.json] PROF[project profile] CFG[project settings] end DE[DocumentationEngine] subgraph Backends WM[WikiManager\nwiki + domains + index] RM[ReadmeManager\nREADME + CONTRIBUTING] AM[AgentResourcesManager\nAGENTS.md + llms.txt + CONTEXT.md] MAN[DocManifest] end subgraph Outputs W[(wiki/**)] R[(README.md)] A[(AGENTS.md / llms.txt)] M[(doc_manifest.json)] end KB --> DE DG --> DE DM --> DE PROF --> DE CFG --> DE DE --> WM --> W DE --> RM --> R DE --> AM --> A DE --> MAN --> M WM -.metadata.-> MAN RM -.metadata.-> MAN AM -.metadata.-> MAN ``` ### Proposed module layout ```txt codx/junior/wiki/ # (rename/alias to codx/junior/docs/ once stable) ├── documentation_engine.py # NEW → orchestrator (public entry point) ├── resources/ │ ├── base_resource.py # NEW → abstract Resource (audience, path, build, hash) │ ├── readme_resource.py # NEW │ ├── contributing_resource.py # NEW │ ├── agents_md_resource.py # NEW │ ├── llms_txt_resource.py # NEW │ └── context_resource.py # NEW ├── wiki_manager.py # existing → becomes the wiki backend ├── wiki_domains.py # existing ├── wiki_index.py # existing ├── doc_manifest.py # NEW → tracks staleness of every resource └── model.py # extend with ResourceManifest, ResourceSpec ``` ### The `Resource` contract Every resource implements the same tiny interface, so the engine can loop over them uniformly and the manifest can always answer *"is this stale?"*. ```py codx/junior/wiki/resources/base_resource.py from abc import ABC, abstractmethod from pathlib import Path from typing import Dict, List class DocumentationResource(ABC): """A single generated documentation artifact.""" spec_id: str audience: str # "human" | "agent" | "both" output_path: Path @abstractmethod def inputs_hash(self) -> str: """Hash of everything that affects this resource (files it reads).""" @abstractmethod def build(self, context: "DocContext") -> str: """Generate the resource content.""" @abstractmethod def affected_by(self, changed_file: str) -> bool: """Return True if a source file change should refresh this resource.""" ``` --- ## 4. How this maps to the current code | Capability | Current status | Location | Gap to close | |------------|----------------|----------|--------------| | Category tree | ✅ Working | `WikiManager.create_wiki_tree` | — | | Per-file wiki page | ✅ Working | `WikiManager.create_wiki_document` | — | | Category/build/rebuild | ✅ Working | `WikiManager.build_wiki_category` / `rebuild_wiki` | — | | Home page | ✅ Working | `WikiManager.build_wiki_home` | — | | Domain pages | ✅ Working | `WikiDomains.build_domain_page` | — | | Dependency graph | ✅ Working | `DependencyGraph` | — | | Wiki index + Milvus | ✅ Working | `WikiIndex.build` / `index_to_milvus` | — | | Full pipeline (BG) | ⚠️ Disabled | `background.process_project_wiki` | Re-enable behind a low-AI budget guard | | Session `update_wiki` | ⚠️ Legacy | `WikiEngine.update_wiki` | Consolidate into the engine | | `KnowledgeWiki` | ❌ Stub | `knowledge_wiki.py` | Remove or re-implement on top of the engine | | `process_wiki_changes` | ❌ No-op | `WikiEngine` | Implement as "refresh stale resources" | | **README generation** | ❌ Missing | — | `ReadmeManager` | | **AGENTS.md generation** | ❌ Missing | — | `AgentResourcesManager` | | **llms.txt generation** | ❌ Missing | — | `AgentResourcesManager` | | **Unified manifest** | ❌ Missing | — | `DocManifest` | | API control surface | ⚠️ Partial | `api/wiki.py` | Add `/api/docs/*` endpoints | --- ## 5. The pipeline The engine exposes three verbs: **`plan` → `build` → `refresh`**. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant Caller participant DE as DocumentationEngine participant DG as DependencyGraph participant WM as WikiManager participant RM as ReadmeManager participant AM as AgentResources participant MAN as DocManifest Caller->>DE: plan() DE->>DG: build/load graph DE->>WM: detect domains (domain_map) DE-->>Caller: [ResourceSpec] + audience + staleness Caller->>DE: build(targets) par human DE->>WM: wiki home, categories, domains, modules and agent DE->>AM: AGENTS.md, llms.txt, CONTEXT.md and readme DE->>RM: README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md end DE->>MAN: save manifest (hash + timestamp) DE-->>Caller: DocManifest Note over Caller,DE: later — a file changes Caller->>DE: refresh(changed_file) DE->>DG: update graph for file DE->>MAN: which resources are affected? DE->>WM: rebuild only affected wiki pages DE->>AM: refresh AGENTS.md "Where things live" if a domain moved DE-->>Caller: updated manifest diff ``` ### Triggers | Trigger | Scope | Where | |---------|-------|-------| | File saved (watcher) | The file's wiki page + affected domain pages | `ChangeManager.process_project_change` | | Manually requested | Any subset via API | `api/docs.py` (new) | | Scheduled | Full rebuild, budget-guarded | `background.check_projects_wiki` | | Project created | Bootstrap all resources | project discovery | > **Budget guard:** the full pipeline is AI-heavy (each page is an LLM call). > Keep `check_projects_wiki` disabled by default and gate it behind > `project_wiki` **and** an explicit `docs_auto_rebuild` flag + a max-tokens budget. --- ## 6. Human vs agent — same facts, different shape The engine generates both from the **same context**, then presents it differently: | Aspect | Human output | Agent output | |--------|--------------|--------------| | Length | Long, narrative | Short, tabular | | Diagrams | Mermaid charts | Mermaid left as-is (agents read it) | | Links | Relative wiki links | Absolute, stable paths | | Emphasis | *Why* & concepts | *Where* & exact commands | | Examples | Full snippets | File path + entry point | | Tone | Onboarding | Rules, do/don't | | Cache key | Content hash | Content hash |
Example — the same "Billing" domain for two audiences **Human (wiki/domains/billing.md)** ```md # Billing ## Overview The billing domain owns subscriptions, invoices and payment reconciliation… ## Entry Points - `billing/api.py` → HTTP entry points - `billing/service.py` → business logic ``` **Agent (AGENTS.md extract)** ```md ## Where things live - Billing → `billing/` → entry `billing/api.py` → tests `tests/billing/` ## Don't - Don't call `billing.service` outside the billing domain; use `billing.api`. ```
--- ## 7. Configuration Extend `CODXJuniorSettings` with an explicit **documentation targets** block, so a project declares which resources it wants. Defaults keep current behaviour. ```py codx/junior/settings.py # Existing project_wiki: Optional[bool] = Field(default=False) project_wiki_path: Optional[str] = Field(default=None) wiki_model: str = Field(default="") # New — documentation targets docs_enabled: bool = Field(default=False) docs_auto_rebuild: bool = Field(default=False) # budget-guarded background loop docs_targets: List[str] = Field( # which resources to generate default=["wiki", "readme", "agents_md", "llms_txt"] ) docs_user_language: str = Field(default="English") docs_instructions: str = Field(default="") # free-text steering ``` --- ## 8. Control surface (API) New router `codx/junior/api/docs.py`, keeping the existing `/wiki-engine/*` endpoints working. | Method | Endpoint | Purpose | |--------|----------|---------| | `GET` | `/api/docs/plan` | List resources, audience and staleness | | `POST` | `/api/docs/build` | Build all (or a subset) | | `POST` | `/api/docs/refresh` | Refresh stale resources only | | `GET` | `/api/docs/manifest` | Return `doc_manifest.json` | | `GET` | `/api/docs/{resource}` | Raw content of one resource | Socket.IO: reuse `codx-junior-wiki` and emit `docs` progress events for each resource. --- ## 9. Implementation plan ```mermaid flowchart LR A[1. DocManifest + resource base] --> B[2. Wrap WikiManager as a Resource] B --> C[3. ReadmeManager] C --> D[4. AgentResourcesManager\nAGENTS.md / llms.txt / CONTEXT.md] D --> E[5. DocumentationEngine orchestrator] E --> F[6. api/docs.py] F --> G[7. Wire watcher + budget-guarded scheduler] ``` 1. **Manifest + base** — `doc_manifest.py`, `resources/base_resource.py`, extend `model.py`. 2. **Wiki as a resource** — thin adapter over `WikiManager` (no behaviour change). 3. **ReadmeManager** — `README.md` + `CONTRIBUTING.md`. 4. **AgentResourcesManager** — `AGENTS.md`, `llms.txt`, `CONTEXT.md`. 5. **DocumentationEngine** — `plan` / `build` / `refresh`. 6. **API** — `api/docs.py`, keep `/wiki-engine/*` as aliases. 7. **Automation** — hook `ChangeManager`, re-enable scheduler behind `docs_auto_rebuild`. 8. **Cleanup** — retire the `KnowledgeWiki` stub and fold `WikiEngine.update_wiki` into the engine. --- ## 10. Definition of done A project is considered **documented** when, on any commit: - [ ] `README.md` explains what the project is and how to run it. - [ ] `AGENTS.md` gives an agent the build/test commands and boundaries. - [ ] `llms.txt` links to the full documentation set. - [ ] The wiki home, every domain page and every module page reflect current code. - [ ] `doc_manifest.json` shows no stale resources (all hashes match). - [ ] The wiki index is pushed to Milvus so RAG answers cite current docs. --- *Made with ❤️ by codx-junior* ``` Let me note the key findings and how the document connects to the existing code. ## Summary I explored the existing documentation machinery in codx-junior and wrote a spec for the missing unifying engine. ### What already exists (and works) - **`WikiManager`** — AI-built category tree, per-file wiki pages, home page, rebuild, MkDocs/VitePress config. - **`WikiDomains` / `WikiIndex` / `DependencyGraph`** — domain detection, domain pages, machine index + Milvus indexing. - **`background.process_project_wiki`** — full pipeline (currently disabled). - **`api/wiki.py`** — `/wiki` + `/wiki-engine/*` endpoints and the `codx-junior-wiki` socket events. ### What's missing for "humans **and** agents" - No **README generation** (only read via `FileEngine.get_readme`). - No **agent resources**: `AGENTS.md`, `llms.txt`, `CONTEXT.md`. - No **orchestrator** or **manifest** tracking which resources exist and are stale. - Dead/stub code: `KnowledgeWiki` (stub), `WikiEngine.process_wiki_changes` (no-op). ### What the document delivers - A single **`DocumentationEngine`** with `plan / build / refresh` verbs. - A uniform **`DocumentationResource`** contract (`audience`, `output_path`, `build`, `affected_by`). - A **resource catalog** split by audience (Human / Agent / Shared), each with concrete paths and section templates. - A **mapping table** tying every capability to its current file and the gap to close. - A staged **implementation plan** and a **definition of done**. Two things worth confirming before this becomes code: 1. **Naming/location** — I placed the spec in `codx/junior/wiki/DOCUMENTATION_ENGINE.md` and proposed the engine live alongside `wiki/` (possibly renamed `docs/`). Do you prefer an existing docs folder? 2. **Scheduler policy** — the full pipeline is AI-heavy and currently disabled in `background.py`. The spec gates it behind a new `docs_auto_rebuild` flag; confirm that's the intended budget guard. Want me to move on to **step 1** (create `doc_manifest.py`, `resources/base_resource.py` and extend `model.py`), or adjust the spec first?
